subject: ACME POC: post-call recap + integration/implementation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, ACME Eng <eng@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: ACME POC — post-call recap + success criteria (next steps)

Thanks everyone for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps for the POC/trial: 

Summary of needs (as we heard it):
- Evaluate Redwood inference for question-answering over internal knowledge base (search + RAG).
- Quality threshold: ~F1/ROUGE target (we'll rely on your eval set); success is parity or better vs current baseline.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for single-turn queries at expected load (concurrent clients ~25).
- Security: VPC/private deployment or strict network controls + audit logs.

Proposed success criteria for the POC (please confirm or update):
1) Latency: p95 under 300ms for 512-token context on standard instance during 25 concurrent users.
2) Quality: top-1 answer accuracy >= baseline on your 500-sample eval set.
3) Stability: no more than 1 incident requiring restart during a 2-week test window.
4) Integration: SDK-based embed + streaming generation working end-to-end with your UI.

Owners and timeline (proposed):
- Kickoff + environment access: Dec 6 (ACME provides network/K8s credentials or VPC peering). Owner: Tom Rivers (ACME).
- Integration spike (SDK + sample routes): Dec 6-10 (Redwood eng: Dev Patel).
- Evaluation run & tuning: Dec 11-17 (joint).
- Wrap + decision: week of Dec 20.

Integration notes / ask from Redwood:
- We'll provide a short SDK package and a minimal Node/Go example that shows streaming + function/tool calling for structured outputs.
- Please share your eval dataset (anonymized) and a test service endpoint we can use for end-to-end verification.

Attachments: acme_poc_mop_v1.pdf, redwood_sdk_integration_guide.zip (integration examples + sample scripts).

Next steps (action items):
- Jane/Tom: confirm success criteria above and confirm Dec 6 kickoff.
- ACME: share eval set + network access details before Dec 6.
- Redwood (Dev): prepare SDK sample and schedule 1-hr kickoff demo for the integration spike.

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your priorities.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — recap looks right. Quick confirmations and clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed success criteria (with clarifications):
- Latency: p95 < 300ms is target; we can tolerate up to 400ms for initial runs but want to optimize. Important: include cold-start behavior in measurement.
- Quality: we'll provide a 500-sample eval set (anonymized) and a small secondary set for hallucination checks.
- Stability: agreed. Please include monitoring hooks (Prometheus metrics or similar) so our SRE can verify.

Security/network: we prefer VPC peering and customer-managed keys. We will share a minimal set of network rules and a service-account key for the test cluster.

Timeline: Dec 6 kickoff works for us. Tom will own environment access and will send initial credentials by EOD Dec 3.

Owners:
- ACME Eng owner: Tom Rivers (tom.rivers@acme.com) — primary for env and test harness.
- Product evaluation: Jane Doe (me) — success criteria & final sign-off.

I attached a short spreadsheet (acme_requirements.xlsx) with a few additional compliance notes and our preferred test matrix (concurrency/seq length).

We look forward to the SDK examples — please make sure the streaming example demonstrates partial tokens and a graceful reconnect strategy.

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC — integration plan & implementation steps (SDK, streaming, tool calling)

Appreciate the confirmations — below is a practical integration plan and implementation checklist for the spike. Dev (cc) will be our technical lead for the spike; I included concrete API/SDK notes you can pass to your eng team.

Integration plan (spike goals):
- Goal A: Get a minimal end-to-end flow working: embed -> retrieval -> streaming generation in your UI.
- Goal B: Validate latency at target concurrency and run the eval set.
- Goal C: Validate VPC connectivity + audit logs.

Implementation steps (detailed):
1) Environment & access (before kickoff)
   - ACME provides VPC peering info or test cluster creds (Tom).
   - Redwood will provision a trial tenant and create an API key scoped to the POC.

2) SDK & examples (Dev Patel)
   - We'll hand over a lightweight SDK (Node + Go) that wraps our REST endpoints and supports streaming responses via SSE/HTTP chunking and WebSocket (if preferred).
   - Example endpoints included: /v1/generate (streaming), /v1/embeddings, /v1/models/list, /v1/tool-call
   - SDK features: automatic reconnect with exponential backoff, chunk assembly for partial tokens, and built-in instrumentation hooks (latency, token counts).

3) API notes and sample curl / Node snippets
   - Streaming (curl):
     curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" \n       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n       https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n       -d '{"model":"redwood-1.3","input":"<prompt>","stream":true}'

   - Node (streaming) quick example (pseudo):
     const res = await sdk.generate({model: 'redwood-1.3', input, stream: true});
     res.on('data', chunk => { /* update UI with partial tokens */ });

   - Embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings with batching support; recommended batch size 64 for latency/cost tradeoff.

4) Tool calling / structured outputs
   - If you need structured extraction or tool invocation, use the /v1/tool-call endpoint. Example payload includes schema and allowed tool list; SDK maps tools to HTTP callbacks.
   - We'll provide one example where the model returns a JSON payload describing an action; Redwood runtime will validate JSON shape if schema provided.

5) Observability & metrics
   - We'll expose Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint for the POC tenant (latency histograms, token counts, batch sizes).
   - Log samples and audit logs (per-request metadata) will be available for manual review.

6) Testing plan
   - Day 0 (kickoff): install SDK, run hello-world streaming flow.
   - Days 1-3: integration spike — instrument metrics and run a small load test.
   - Days 4-7: run full eval suite (your 500 samples).

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood technical lead: Dev Patel (dev.patel@redwood.com) — spike owner and primary for troubleshooting.
- Redwood sales/SE: Marissa Cole — scheduling and success criteria.
- ACME technical owner: Tom Rivers (tom.rivers@acme.com).

Support during spike
- We'll allocate a 3-hour block on Day 1 for pairing/debugging and stand by for Slack/Zoom.

Docs & links
- SDK package + examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cACME-poc
- HubSpot record: HS-ACME-7894

Notes on cost and token accounting
- For the spike we will provide a trial credit bucket. Token usage will be reported daily and we will recommend batching/kv-cache settings if token spend exceeds expected.

If this looks good, we'll schedule the kickoff for Dec 6 at 10:00am PT and Dev will send the SDK package before the meeting.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
